hints.content:
The basic function $\sin(x)$ intersects its midline at $(0,0)$ and has a maximum point at $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},1\right)$.

$\qquad$![](${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/06941548a579199b78346bf8e7ed0476.png)

Let's transform $\pink{\sin(x)}$ to $\blue{0.5\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}x+\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right)-2}$ step by step and see how the graph changes along the way.

The transformation from $\pink{\sin(x)}$ to $\green{\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}x\right)}$ is a horizontal shrink by a factor of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$, so the maximum point's horizontal distance from the origin is shrunk from $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ to $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\cdot\dfrac{3}{\pi}=1.5$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

The transformation from $\green{\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}x\right)}$ to $\red{0.5\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}x\right)}$ is a vertical shrink by a factor of $2$, so the maximum point's vertical distance from the origin is shrunk from $1$ to $0.5$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 2]]

options.alt: A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (pi over two, one). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (one and one half, one).

A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by one and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (one and one half, one). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (one and one half, one half).

hints.content: The transformation from $\red{0.5\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}x\right)}$ to $\blue{0.5\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}x+\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right)-2}$, which is equivalent to $0.5\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}(x+4)\right)-2$, is a translation to the left by $4$ units and a translation downwards by $2$ units.

As a result of these transformations, the intersection point with the midline is now at $\left(-4,-2\right)$ and the maximum point is at $(-2.5,-1.5)$.

The resulting graph looks as follows:

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A graph of a trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by one and the y axis scales by one. There is a point on the graph at the midline at (negative four, negative two) and a point on the maximum next to the mentioned point at (negative two and one half, negative one and one half).

question.content:
**Graph $g(x)=0.5\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}x+\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right)-2$ in the interactive widget.**  
*Note that one moveable point always defines an extremum point in the graph and the other point always defines a neighbouring intersection with the midline.*
